events.text: A letter from {npc}, the strokes of light wobbling: the beds are clouds that will not stay still, the dew is grey, and the older children of the gods take the good seats. {He} does not say {he} wants to come home. {He} says it four times without saying it.

effects.log: You write three tablets of light and break two. The one you send says you are proud, and means it.

choices.text: Send an offering with the letter

mem.note: sent silver to me at school

effects.log: An offering goes with the letter. Somewhere a cook of the pantheon is about to be very well thanked for extra honey cakes.
Your letter is short and has no warmth in it. The next letter you get back is neater, and shorter too.
You cross the sky and bring {npc} home. The school does not keep a place for a child who leaves.

events.text: {npc}'s teacher crosses the sky in person, which gods of the school never do, to ask for {npc} as a direct disciple: the one who learns the hymns the others are not taught. It means fewer letters home, and much more.

mem.note: let me become a direct disciple

effects.log: The master bows to you as an equal. {npc} kneels to the master as a disciple. Both of them look terrified.
The master leaves without arguing. {npc} does not speak to you for a week.

events.text: A tablet sealed with a god's own sigil: {npc} has been chosen as a direct disciple, if the family allows it. The other children of the gods have already heard. Half are jealous. The other half are relieved it was not them.

effects.log: You seal your answer with your own sigil. {npc} writes back four tablets in one night.
{npc} writes back one word: yes. Then another page about how surprised {he} was to be asked.
The master does not ask twice. Masters never do.
